significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) relation: across the named materials-model classes, a "two-to-three-dimensional manifold" would jointly predict group, period, and atomic-property variation beyond composition co-occurrence, while embedding substitutions would causally shift formation-energy or band-gap predictions in the corresponding chemical direction. This establishes a definite representational phenomenon and a limited mechanism linking element geometry to predictions; it constrains expected neighborhoods, decodability, and intervention effects, but it does not establish that the models implement the underlying physical mechanisms of electronegativity or valence. Verified false would distinguishably rule out this low-dimensional linear account and its causal-swap consequence, although nonlinear or distributed scientific representations would remain possible; this matters because models such as Roost and CGCNN rely on learned element representations for property prediction. In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of whether scientific concepts are represented would not earn this score—the extra value comes from the specific dimensionality, property-axis coupling, co-occurrence dissociation, and behavioral consequence—yet recovering periodic organization is still close to the obvious first materials-embedding hypothesis, so the increment is moderate.

reach.justification: The claim supplies named handles: the "group-neighborhood consistency score," property-axis explained variance, and the element-embedding substitution intervention, which could be used to audit whether a materials model has learned chemically organized element representations. These are principally post-hoc diagnostics rather than validated ex-ante predictors: "informing their reliability for extrapolative discovery" does not itself assert that the scores forecast under-sampled-chemistry failures before they occur. After re-extracting embeddings, however, the asserted relation predicts that crystal graph networks and composition transformers should again exhibit a two-to-three-dimensional group/period manifold with electronegativity and size axes, so more than a model-specific search procedure transfers; likely downstream users include interpretability researchers and materials-model auditors, though no concrete deployment gate is claimed. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score, because the topic alone provides neither these diagnostics nor a transferable manifold relation; the reach comes from those claim-specific handles rather than from materials science as an application area.
